title: Store a Slice in a Struct
goal: Choose the struct design that avoids cloning string data.
hints: Check whether `Header` needs to own its data or if it can view `line`.
Storing `&'a str` avoids heap allocations entirely.
explanation: `Header<'a>` holds a slice reference (`&'a str`) borrowed directly from `line`. Using `Header<'_>` in the return signature allows lifetime elision to connect `Header` to the lifetime of `line`. Candidate 2 creates a local owned `String` and returns a reference to it (`&owned`), which fails to compile because `owned` is dropped when `parse_header` returns. Candidate 3 requires `Header<'static>`, which fails to compile because `line` is borrowed with a non-static lifetime.
